title: 'It Has Been Very Difficult': Suryakumar Yadav Opens Up After India Snub
excerpt: Dropped months after captaining India to a T20 World Cup title defence, the 36-year-old credited his wife Devisha and his baby daughter with helping him rediscover his love for the game before leading Mumbai in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy.
body:
• Suryakumar Yadav, 36, has spoken publicly for the first time about being dropped from India's T20I side months after captaining the team to a successful T20 World Cup title defence in March.
  • He credited a conversation with his wife Devisha Shetty — and the birth of his baby girl during the IPL in May — with helping him rediscover the love for cricket he had as a 15-year-old.
  • Suryakumar returns to competitive cricket as Mumbai captain in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, starting November 14 against Hyderabad at Eden Gardens, Kolkata.
  • He has 113 T20I appearances and, per SportsTak, is closing in on 10,000 runs in T20 cricket; Shreyas Iyer has taken over India's T20I leadership.

Suryakumar Yadav has admitted that being dropped from the India team he led to a T20 World Cup title only months earlier hit him hard — and that his way back ran through a conversation with his wife and a return to the habits of a teenager. The 36-year-old spoke to the media on November 10 at a Mumbai Cricket Association event honouring the T20 Mumbai League champions, in his first extended public remarks since losing his place, according to India Today's report of his comments to PTI.

"Post the T20 World Cup win, it has been a little difficult. I don't want to run away from that fact."

— Suryakumar Yadav

From World Cup Captain to Out of the Side

Suryakumar captained India to a successful T20 World Cup title defence on home soil in March 2026. A lean patch with the bat and an underwhelming IPL season followed, and the BCCI moved on from him ahead of the England tour, with Shreyas Iyer taking over the leadership. He has 113 T20I appearances, played only local club games and the Mumbai T20 League in the months since, missed the Ranji Trophy season, and last played competitive cricket in May, SportsTak reported. We covered his appointment as Mumbai's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy captain in our earlier report on the Mumbai squad.

The Conversation That Turned It

Two things changed his outlook, he said. During the IPL he was blessed with a baby girl in May, and his focus shifted completely towards her. And in a frank discussion, his wife Devisha Shetty told him he needed to bring back the love and passion for the game he had as a 15-year-old who wanted to represent Mumbai in Under-15 cricket. He has since gone back to the routines of 10 to 15 years ago — training again with the same approach — and says everything is back to normal, as Cricbuzz reported.

His advice to Mumbai's youngsters at the event ran on the same line: the first goal should be to play for Mumbai and earn that cap, not to play in the IPL. He said he would be happy to spend time with the young players in the dressing room, pass on what 16 years with the association have taught him, and lead the side.

What Comes Next

The comeback begins on Saturday, November 14, when Mumbai open their Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy campaign against Hyderabad at Eden Gardens in Kolkata, with Suryakumar as captain. His stated goal is narrow and familiar: win games for Mumbai and win the championship for Mumbai. A strong tournament is also the only route back into the India conversation — he is, per SportsTak, closing in on 10,000 T20 runs — but by his own account, that is no longer the thought he starts with. The thought he starts with is the one he had at 15.
